title: Per-token electricity + amortization scenario sheet (A10 L4 A100 H100)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet estimates the electricity and GPU-amortization component of $/token for four common accelerator classes (A10, L4, A100, H100). The goal is to provide a lightweight scenario matrix (utilization bands) to feed into token-econ simulations and to inform instance selection guidance for different utilization profiles and commitment levels.

High-level summary (headline takeaways):
- For fully utilized racks (steady 24/7 throughput) amortization is the dominant component of $/token for A100/H100.
- For low-utilization, small-instance use (bursty endpoints, dev), amortization balloons and smaller-capex GPUs (L4/A10) often win on $/token.
- Electricity is generally a rounding term at $0.12/kWh in our baseline — amortization drives differences between instance families.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Electricity price: $0.12 per kWh.
- Accounting: simple straight-line amortization; monthly amortization is treated as fixed cost per GPU (includes tax, rack, basic PSU/cooling allocation). Hours/month = 730.
- Power draw (typical active): A10 150 W, L4 65 W, A100 400 W, H100 500 W.
- Baseline throughput (representative model mix, single-GPU steady-state tokens/s): A10 700 t/s, L4 480 t/s, A100 2600 t/s, H100 3200 t/s.
- Monthly amortization (examples, USD): A10 $700, L4 $450, A100 $4000, H100 $9000.
- Simple linear scaling assumptions used for utilization bands (notes below).

Method / formula (applied to every scenario):
- Electricity $/token = electricity_price * (power_W / 1000) / (tokens_per_second * 3600)
- Amortization $/token = (monthly_amort / 730) / (tokens_per_second * 3600)
- Total $/token = electricity $/token + amortization $/token

Baseline (100% effective tokens/s):
Columns: gpu, power_W, tokens_s, monthly_amort, elec_per_token($), amort_per_token($), total_per_token($)
A10,150,700,$700,0.00000000714,0.0000003804,0.0000003876
L4,65,480,$450,0.00000000451,0.0000003568,0.0000003613
A100,400,2600,$4000,0.00000000513,0.0000005856,0.0000005907
H100,500,3200,$9000,0.00000000521,0.0000010703,0.0000010755

Low-utilization (30% effective throughput) — simple scaling (tokens/s *0.3, power and amortization treated proportionally for tokens):

L4 (144 t/s): elec 0.0000000150, amort 0.000001189, total 0.000001204

H100 (2240 t/s): elec 0.00000000743, amort 0.000000477, total 0.000000485

Notes on linearity and caveats:
- We used a simplified linear scaling approach for tokens and (for electricity) power. In practice GPU power draw does not scale perfectly linearly with throughput (idle power + dynamic power curve). For rough planning this is okay; for procurement decisions run kernel-level profiler traces.
- Amortization is handled as per-GPU fixed monthly cost. If you place multiple models per GPU (multi-tenant batching) effective tokens/s per GPU increases and amortization/token drops accordingly. Also reserved contracts (committed clusters) shift the amortization line and change per-token math.
- This sheet ignores other infra costs: rack PDU overhead, front-end servers, network, storage, orchestration (k8s nodes), software license fees. Add ~10–30% on top of the GPU+electricity number for conservative TCO.

Quick sensitivity takeaways (rounded):
- If utilization <40%: prefer L4/A10 on $/token in many cases because capex dominates.
- If utilization >70%: large accelerators (A100/H100) often win on $/token for heavy throughput workloads despite higher amortization, because the amortization is diluted across many more tokens.
- Electricity price sensitivity at 0.12 -> 0.24 $/kWh changes totals by a small percent (electricity is a low-order term vs amortization at current assumptions).

Actionable recommendations (next steps for product/ops):
1) For each customer profile (dev / staging / low-qps endpoints / high-throughput inference), map expected tokens/s per cluster and apply this sheet to pick instance family for cost minimization.
2) Run a follow-up micro-benchmark for two representative models (13B & 70B ranges) per GPU to measure real tokens/s and power curves; replace linear assumptions with measured curves.
3) Create a small calculator (spreadsheet) that exposes knobs: electricity_price, monthly_amort per GPU, target_utilization, tokens_per_call, avg_call_rate — to produce $/1000 tokens and hourly cost estimates.
4) For Reserved/Dedicated planning, include committed utilization smoothing: amortization can be reduced by 20–40% under multi-year commitments + higher packing.

Open questions for the team (to resolve in follow-up):
- Should amortization include rack-level shared items (PDUs, switches) or leave those as separate line items?
- Which representative model(s) should we standardize on for per-GPU throughput reference (13B inference, 70B hallucination-heavy, chat with 2k context)?
- Target electricity price sensitivity band for regions (US-West 0.07–0.18; EU 0.20–0.35) — we should produce region-specific tables.

Working artifacts (what this file is feeding):
- token-econ sensitivity simulations (product/optimize pipeline)
- Dedicated capacity pricing proposal drafts

Notes to self (todo):
- import measured power traces from lab-bench (bench-logs/2024-10) and replace linear scaling assumptions.
- add a 2nd sheet with thermal/cooling multipliers and PUE by datacenter class.

(End of sheet)
